title: Toward the summit
hookLine: two weeks to look back over five years and forward to a life
tomorrow: from the top of Nebo, what did Moses see that he'd never enter?

cards: Hikers know the false summit: the ridge that looks like the top, and then there's more trail. This path has two weeks left. Noa leaves for college in about the same.
Saba wants to walk her up the one real hill in their town before she goes, to look back at the houses. She'd rather pack. He's already waiting by the door with two bottles of water.

teach.b: There's a set of psalms with a heading that fits this walk: "A Song of Ascents." Tradition connects them with pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

teach.h: I WILL LIFT UP MINE EYES.
teach.b: One of them opens: "I will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains: from whence shall my help come?"

teach.h: MY HELP COMETH FROM THE LORD.
teach.b: And the next line answers: "My help cometh from the LORD, who made heaven and earth." The looking up is half of it. The other half is knowing where the help comes from on the way.
Near the top of anything long, two things are true at once.
You're nearly there. And the last stretch still has to be walked. So this is a day for looking back, without sorting: the words, the stories, the faces, the lines you kept and the ones you dropped.
The next two weeks gather them up. Something to tell a friend tonight: the psalm about lifting your eyes to the mountains answers its own question in the very next line.

how: The psalms headed 'A Song of Ascents' are sung and studied in Jewish life; the end of a long course of study can be marked with a siyum, a celebration of finishing.

games.q: you're two weeks from finishing something long: a degree, a training, a year of practice. what fits 'nearly there'?
o: stop to look back, then walk the last stretch steadily.
rush the rest; the end is basically already here.
quit now; you've done enough for it to count.
games.why: near the top, two things are true: you're nearly there, and the last stretch still has to be walked. the psalm lifts its eyes and keeps climbing.

practice: Sit quietly, eyes closed, for the whole time. Let this path come back in no order: a word, a story, a face, one line you carried. Don't sort them or judge them; let each one pass, and notice which one stays.
